clue.text: Serious error when a tomb is wrongly identified

definitions.meaning: a bad blunder of real consequence

definitions.text: when a tomb is wrongly identified
definitions.meaning: a burial plot mixed up with another would be an error about a grave

explanation.surface: A cemetery mix-up turns out to be a very serious blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a GRAVE is a tomb, so mistaking one is literally a grave mistake.

clue.text: The divine design yields an unexpected blessing

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the Almighty's purpose
a welcome stroke of luck

explanation.surface: Heaven's plan turning out to be a happy surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GOD'S END: 'end' meaning purpose or design.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome windfall seems sent from heaven; split, it is the Almighty's purpose.

clue.text: First person to construct a water-barrier

explanation.surface: The first man undertaking some engineering on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the first man was named ADAM; 'to construct' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's first man was created before Eve.

clue.text: Perpetual description of Schubert's Unfinished Symphony

definitions.meaning: lasting forever
a work with no conclusion

explanation.surface: A remark about Schubert's famous incomplete symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert's Eighth Symphony is famously unfinished, so it literally lacks an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Never stopping; read literally, a symphony lacking a final movement.

clue.text: Original way to amend an error on a cheque

definitions.meaning: first, earliest

definitions.text: way to amend an error on a cheque
definitions.meaning: a correction on a cheque is signed off with the writer's letters

explanation.surface: A novel way to fix a mistake when writing a cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: A correction on a cheque is validated by writing your initials beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Means first or earliest; also the act of signing with one's initials to approve an alteration.

clue.text: Examine a flower in Hampshire

definitions.meaning: to try out or check
flower means something that flows: a river in the southern English county

explanation.surface: Inspecting a bloom found in a county garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (it flows); the Test runs through Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To try or check; also the name of a chalk stream famed for trout.

clue.text: Shrewd sovereign absorbed at the moment

explanation.surface: A clever monarch lost in thought just now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' looks like 'engrossed', but it puts NOW inside KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and aware, implying more understanding than one shows.

clue.text: Visiting the opera is dirt-cheap

definitions.meaning: setting out to hear some singing
sold for a trifle

explanation.surface: An evening at the opera turns out to be a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being sold at a very low price; literally heading off for some music.

clue.text: Moderate man let a disorderly assembly become volatile

indicators.note: the three words are gathered together in no order, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An even-tempered man lets an unruly crowd turn explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' is a verb giving TEMPER; 'disorderly assembly' makes AMENTAL from MAN LET A.
explanation.definitionFit: Moody and unpredictable, given to sudden swings of mood.

clue.text: Elderly worker, but an experienced one

definitions.meaning: a hand is a labourer, and an old one is aged
a veteran who knows the ropes

explanation.surface: An aged labourer who is also a seasoned veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an aged labourer; idiomatically a veteran with long practice.

clue.text: Where shoppers may get goods reserved

definitions.meaning: inside a shop, where purchases are found
kept back for later, held ready

explanation.surface: Shoppers collecting items that have been set aside for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally inside a shop; idiomatically held back and waiting for the future.

clue.text: Term applied to Christmas by Mr Coward

definitions.meaning: a carol word for the festive season
the playwright Noël Coward's first name

explanation.surface: A playwright supplying a word for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward was an English playwright and wit; his forename is also a festive word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word names the festive season, and it is also the forename of playwright Coward.

clue.text: The French can make an admission

parts.note: le is the French masculine article meaning 'the'

explanation.surface: A French tin is somehow able to confess.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them entry, which the phrasal verb means.

clue.text: Game walk by Long Island politician

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for Long Island, New York

explanation.surface: A Long Island politician going for a sporting stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here means lame, as in a game leg, not a sport; 'by' just links the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame gait is a halting, uneven walk, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: A right to keep property of a stranger

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's goods until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A claim on the possessions of an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIEN is the legal right to hold someone's property as security; 'of' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner or outsider; an extraterrestrial too.

clue.text: Gave instructions on how the line might be drawn

definitions.meaning: governed or decreed

definitions.text: on how the line might be drawn
definitions.meaning: a straight line is drawn with a ruler

explanation.surface: Laying down the law on where a boundary goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Governed or decreed; also marked with lines using a straight edge.

clue.text: Fraudulent practices in the orchestra

definitions.meaning: swindles or rackets
violins, found among the strings

explanation.surface: Scams going on among the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindles are informally so called, and the violins of an orchestra share the word.

clue.text: Chair put right at the end of the living-room

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for right is placed after the room word

parts.note: a lounge is a sitting room

explanation.surface: Instructions for where to place a chair in the sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A reclining garden or poolside seat goes by this name.

clue.text: His hair-colouring would seem to make him an ideal Soviet leader

definitions.text: His hair-colouring would seem to make him an ideal Soviet leader

parts.words: His hair-colouring would seem to make him an ideal Soviet leader
parts.note: a ginger-haired man, read as a communist (red) chief (head)

explanation.surface: A ginger man who looks ready to lead the USSR.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of communism, and a head is a leader, so a ginger-haired person looks a natural Soviet chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with ginger or auburn hair is described by this compound.

clue.text: Man of vision

parts.note: a visionary, or one who sees things in his sleep

explanation.definitionFit: A visionary idealist, or someone seeing images while asleep.

clue.text: Absolutely determined onslaught to win over those in the catacombs, perhaps

definitions.meaning: fully resolved
to make a fixed attack on someone is to set at them
a group of corpses in burial vaults

explanation.surface: A resolute attack to convert the people buried underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings: resolved; a determined assault (making a dead set at someone); and a set, or group, of the dead in catacombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly resolved; a concerted attempt to win someone; and literally a group of corpses.

clue.text: The more elaborate of math emetical propositions?

definitions.note: the clue's plural is the class; the answer is one member of it

indicators.note: an elaborate version is worked up and rearranged, so the two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Asking which of some maths statements is the more complicated one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' rearranges THE MORE; the question mark signals the answer is one example of the propositions named.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement proved from axioms is one of the core propositions of mathematics.

clue.text: Spinner's speed is first-class

definitions.meaning: how fast a spinning top turns: its rate
excellent

explanation.surface: A bowler's pace is rated superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but it is a child's spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent; literally the speed of a spinning toy.

clue.text: Went to bed after leaving work

definitions.meaning: turned in for the night
having stopped working for good, on a pension

explanation.surface: Someone heading to bed after clocking off.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal for turned in for the night; also having given up one's career.

clue.text: He looks on and on into the future

definitions.text: He looks on and on into the future

parts.words: He looks on and on into the future
parts.note: one who watches, and watches far ahead: a prophet

explanation.surface: A man gazing ever onward into what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is literally one who sees ahead.

clue.text: They have a sting in the tail in Aristophanes' play

definitions.text: They have a sting in the tail
definitions.meaning: striped insects whose sting is at the rear
a comedy by the Greek dramatist, about jurors

explanation.surface: A Greek comedy with a nasty twist at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sting in the tail' usually means a nasty twist at the end; here it is literal, about insects.

clue.text: Educational establishment epitomising English style

indicators.note: an epitome is a summary, so only the opening letter of the word stands for it

explanation.surface: A school said to be the very model of Englishness.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is a famous English private school; TON (from French) is fashionable style.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous boarding college near Windsor is a school.

clue.text: Goddess currently found in Oxford

definitions.meaning: the Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic

explanation.surface: A deity now living in the university city.

clue.text: Some go slowly round a Scandinavian city

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Vengeance seems in order

explanation.surface: Revenge appears to be quite proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution, named after the Greek goddess of divine retribution.

clue.text: Young Albert leaves Australia for a European country

parts.note: Al is the short familiar form of Albert

explanation.surface: Young Albert emigrates from Australia to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like travel, but it is a deletion of AL from AUSTRALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna's nation is a central European state.

clue.text: Do carthorses need reharness ing to get to the other side?

definitions.text: to get to the other side?

explanation.surface: A question about tacking up the horses before crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the old riddle 'Why did the chicken cross the road? To get to the other side'.
